text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Cabinet to decide on next withdrawal from West Bank today.
- Commission probing February 4 helicopter collision, in which 73 soldiers were killed, sends out letters of caution to three air force officers and an officer in Northern Command.
- Attorney Yoram Turbowicz shocks Communications Minister Limor Livnat, says no to appointment as Bezeq Communications director-general.
- Trade Minister Natan Sharansky invites representatives of world's largest firms to visit Israel over coming weeks.
- Haifa Chemicals workers reject compromise pact.
- U.S. lawyers to sue Assicurazioni Generali insurance company over refusal to pay Holocaust victims.
- Israeli hotels to get their stars back.
GLOBES
- Drop of 7 percent in sale of apartments in big cities during the last quarter of 1996.
- Knesset, Israel's parliament, rejects bill to cut concession of Israel Electric Co from 10 to six years.
- Africa-Israel directorate to appeal against closing of Ramat Aviv mall on Jewish sabbaths.
HAARETZ

- Israeli army to demand government prevent Palestinian territorial continuity in next troop withdrawal. Government to receive several alternatives for a first-stage withdrawal of from four to 10 percent in the West Bank.
- Labour minister increases supervision on issuance of permits to foreign workers, in effort to reduce their number.
- Avigdor Lieberman, director-general of prime minister's office, calls "Bar-On affair -- an invention".
- New record for dollar: 3.367 shekels.
MAARIV
- Dispute in government over Netanyahu proposal to evacuate 8-10 percent of the West Bank.
- Maariv locates one of the heirs to money deposited in Switzerland.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Directors of six insurance companies convicted of creating a cartel.

- In government today: Stormy discussion expected on further withdrawal. Defence establishment expects next pullout will not be carried out over the weekend. Expectation of an 11-5 vote. Opponents: Ariel Sharon, Rafael Eitan, Zevulun Hammer, Yitzhak Levy and perhaps Yuli Edelstein.

- National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon quoted as saying: "Bibi (Netanyahu) is dangerous to the state of Israel" and "I don't believe a single word that man says". Sharon in response: "I don't relate to gossip".
- Legendary Welsh singer Tom Jones to perform in Israel at end of month.
